image_description: A close-up shot of a fig tree branch featuring multiple figs in various stages of ripeness. There are green, unripe figs with a speckled texture and a dark purple/black ripe fig. The fruits are attached to thick brown woody branches. Green leaves with visible veins are present in the background and foreground. One fig appears to have a slight split or opening near the stem.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pear-shaped fruit with soft, thin skin in green, purple, or brownish coloration.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays fruits matching the description: green unripe figs and a dark purple ripe fig are visible. The shape is consistent with pears/figs.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Smooth to slightly wrinkled texture with matte finish.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin of the green figs shows a characteristic matte, slightly speckled/wrinkled texture typical of real figs. The purple fig also has a matte finish.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated pear shape with tapered form from broad base to narrow stem end.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The green fig in the center-left exhibits the classic pyriform (pear) shape, tapering towards the stem attachment point.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Small ostiole (eye) at bottom of fruit.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bottom tips (ostioles) of the figs are either occluded by leaves, pointing away from the camera, or obscured by the angle. The visible parts are primarily the stem ends and sides.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Narrow stem end contrasting with broad rounded base.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The attachment points to the branch show the narrower stem end, while the body of the fruit bulges out, creating the expected contrast.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Thin, easily bruised skin covering soft interior.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin appears thin and delicate. There is a slight discoloration/split on the central green fig which suggests the soft, easily damaged nature of the skin.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Cut cross-section reveals hollow interior filled with numerous tiny seeds.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: None of the figs in the image are cut open; they are all whole fruits on the tree.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Sweet, pink to amber-colored fleshy pulp surrounding seeds.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Interior pulp is not visible as no fruit is cut.
Texture of the interior cannot be visually confirmed without a cut cross-section or tactile interaction.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight smearing or 'painterly' quality in the out-of-focus background leaves. The transition between the branch and the background foliage is slightly soft, lacking crisp occlusion boundaries, which is common in AI generation but could also be depth-of-field blur.

artifact_observations.location: Stem attachment of the central green fig
artifact_observations.reasoning: The connection point between the central green fig and its stem/branch looks slightly ambiguous. The stem seems to merge into the fruit skin rather than attaching distinctly, suggesting a minor fusion artifact.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the stem attachments. AI often struggles with how thin stems connect to bulky fruits, resulting in 'mushy' connections. Verify if the classifier confirms 'fig' specifically, as unripe figs can resemble small pears or guavas. Check if the background blur is natural optical bokeh or AI-generated smearing.
